newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sasol welcomes environmental report.
newsitem.headline: Sasol welcomes environmental report.

text.p: South African fuels firm Sasol Ltd on Monday welcomed an environmental report that it said showed a proposed strip mine would have an acceptable level of ecological impact.

The independent Environmental Management Programme Report indicated that the design of the Sigma North West colliery, to be sited at Vaal River near Sasolburg in the Orange Free State, meant many of most severe environmental impacts would be avoided, the firm said.

The report said that with effective management the strip mine would have low to moderate impact on noise and dust levels, would pose no risk to water quality and would not affect wetlands of national importance.
However, the report did say the loss of wetlands nationwide, to which this small loss would add, was a highly negative factor.
It also said the negative impact on fish life in the Vaal River would be high during the early years of the mine.
"We are pleased that the report has not unearthed insurmountable environmental challenges. We are also committed to implementing the reports recommendations," said Sasol managing director Pieter Cox.
Cox said the report committed the firm to "substantial investment in mitigating measures".
Sasol wants to develop the strip mine as its Sigma underground operation is nearing the ends of its working life.
The planned mine would take the form of three trenches, hidden from view by berms -- large earthen mounds planted with trees. The pits would be filled in once they are mined out.
However, the process of gaining official approval for the mine was far from complete, Sasol said.
The mine aimed to produce 4.2 million tons of sub-bituminous coal a year for use as feedstock in its Sasolburg chemical plant.
